lesson-intro.text: Nobody draws every brick in a wall. A few here and there, and the eye fills in the rest. Watch this old window take shape, then let the light into yours.

ledge.text: Start at the bottom with the ledge: one long, flat box with soft corners.

frame.text: The frame stands on the ledge. Each side goes up and curves in to meet at the top.

arch.text: A curved band of brick sits on the frame. From each foot, step out, then curve up to the top.

wedges.text: Six short lines cut the band into seven wedges. They fan out like wheel spokes.

posts.text: Under each end of the band, a straight post drops down to the ledge.

glass.text: Next, the glass: two rounded panes on top, two tall ones below. The gaps make a cross.

right-bricks.text: Now a few bricks. Three on the right, stepping in and out like a real wall.

left-bricks.text: Two more at the top left, and one on its own near the bottom.

left-stem.text: A vine climbs the left side. Draw its long wavy stem from the bottom up.

top-leaves.text: A leaf caps the stem. Three more sprout just below it, two left and one right.

lower-leaves.text: Four leaves down the lower half, swapping sides as they go.

right-vine.text: Then a shorter vine on the right: its stem first, then four leaves.

cream.text: Cream for the frame and the two posts.

pink-gray.text: Pink for the wedges of the arch and the six bricks. The ledge is gray.

greens.text: Green and pale green for the leaves, mixed along both vines.

lesson-outro.text: Your window is done, and the vines are already climbing past it. What's the view from inside?
